title: Research: exact frame search certifies #741 and #626 providers frame-optimal (rediscovers #741; negative result)
head: d8c8b40ab0a95b6d77389e6726d86dddb60fb53c
body:
**Update: current selected word (#741).** Rebased on main after #741 merged. I gave CP-SAT PR699's SW4 word (`d232183f…`), using the admissible model with the audit's hpe cone caps and fixed tail frames. In 27 s it returned `OPTIMAL` with exactly #741's profile `{1:2556,2:334,3:430,4:194,5:56,8:8}`, so the solver rediscovers #741's gain without guidance. `check_sw4.py` applies #741's recipe and reproduces its pinned output hash `e7804702…`. The LP optimum over all frame assignments then equals #741's weight: 18155.950422 linear and 18219.665540 exact-root at #741's complex root, with gaps under 1e-9. So **no frame-only change of the selected word can raise κ**; PR699's frame slack (6.90 units) is exactly what #741 recovered. Six commuting-reorder restarts on #741, each re-solved by the LP, gave no gain. The receipt is `RESULT-SW4.json`. This work does not touch the R420/R439 bit or E8 lines (#789/#790/#792, #765/#767/#770).

**Negative result, scoped. No κ change.** By Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani), with substantial AI assistance (an AI coding agent wrote the search code and ran the experiments).

The complex side binds the selected κ. In the 64 jp8 calls, unit climbs make up 160,768 of the 181,659 rank-1 children. Paid children are exactly the frame climbs that `hpe_audit_and_transport.py::climb` counts, and the scalar program never reads frames. So I treated every A/B/tail gate frame of the selected provider words as a variable and searched all of them exactly.

**Result.** For #626's `jp8` and `ck` words (content hashes pinned in `complex-k492-owner-repair/data/SPEC.json`, rebuilt fresh by the package's `verify.py`), the paid profile is optimal over every frame assignment of the fixed gate sequence:

| word | gates | input weight | LP optimum (HiGHS) | CP-SAT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| jp8 | 4471 | 18475.029780700 | 18475.029780701 | OPTIMAL, same value |
| ck | 4507 | 18568.580702034 | 18568.580702035 | OPTIMAL, same value |

The weight is the linearised moment, Σ d·ln(48/d). Each word's rank mass is fixed by its widths, so at the selected root a* the exact criterion is Σ d·(73/d)^a*. That weight is also LP-optimal at the input (gap below 1e-9). The model relaxes the audit: it omits the hpe cone caps and cold_end conditions and leaves tail frames free. So no frame regroup, coalescence or promotion recipe of any size can raise κ on these words. Lifting every frame to its greatest feasible value costs +3.8%. Annealing over commuting reorders (the `build_gate_moves.py` rule), followed by an exact frame re-solve, gave no gain in 11 restarts (`ORDER-SEARCH.json`). That is a sample, not a proof for all orders.

**Context for κ > 0.01.** Jensen's inequality gives a ≤ −ln p / E_mass[ln(73/r)]. At the current deficit (2560 / 523264), a ≥ 0.01 needs a mass-weighted geometric-mean child rank of at least 44.7; today it is 3.66. At today's child ranks it would instead need a deficit of at least 15,425 (6.0×). Reaching it needs new scalar structure, not frame bookkeeping. About 1,700 of jp8's 2,512 rank-1 climbs are helper unit climbs.

**Files.** `research/frame-lift-search/` contains the model, the LP/CP-SAT solvers, the order search, `RESULT.json` and `ORDER-SEARCH.json`. `tests/test_frame_lift_search.py` checks the lattice model on the in-repo #571 prefix word. There is also a one-line experiment-log link.

**Verification.** `check.py` ran on a fresh `complex-k492-owner-repair/verify.py` rebuild (Linux, Python 3.13) and reports `PASS_FRAME_ONLY_LP_OPTIMAL_FOR_SELECTED_PROVIDERS`. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_frame_lift_search` passes. I did not run `make verify`: no generator, certificate or selected-record file changed.

**Limits.** HiGHS is a floating-point LP, not an exact rational dual certificate, and CP-SAT's `OPTIMAL` comes without a proof log. The scalar program, helper count, dispatch, hosting and bit supplier are out of scope.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
